### Fixed
- The kagent controller metrics `Service` the connectivity chart renders (`<release>-kagent-controller-metrics`, the target of its `ServiceMonitor`) selected the controller pods with the connectivity release's own `app.kubernetes.io/instance` label. Under the retired standalone umbrella every subchart shared one release name, so that matched; under the meta chart each component is its own release — the kagent pods carry `app.kubernetes.io/instance: kagent`, the component key the meta chart fixes as the release name — and the Service had no endpoints: the controller was never scraped on any installation with kagent and the monitors on (#305). The selector now names kagent's release through the new connectivity helper `agent-platform.kagent.releaseName`; the fallbacks of the controller route's backend host, the UI route's Service and the oauth2-proxy Service (`kagent.fullnameOverride` / `kagent.oauth2-proxy.fullnameOverride`, pinned in values.yaml, else `.Release.Name`) go through `agent-platform.kagent.fullname` / the release-name helper too — the same wrong assumption, latent behind the pins. No compatibility knob: the meta chart is the chart's only consumer. **No installation needs to act**: the Service's selector changes (a Service update, no pod rolls) and kagent controller scraping starts working; every other object is byte-identical. `make verify-global` asserts the selector and that no kagent template falls back to `.Release.Name`.
- A first `helm install` with `components.kagent.enabled` on a cluster without the `kagent` namespace deadlocked: the kagent chart installs into `kagent.namespaceOverride` while its `HelmRelease` targets the platform namespace (so `install.createNamespace` never creates `kagent`), and the one chart object that does create it — the connectivity chart's `Namespace` — sits in a release that `dependsOn` kagent. Every kagent attempt failed with `namespaces "kagent" not found` until the retries were exhausted, everything behind kagent waited, `helm install --wait` timed out (#306). With the bundled engine the meta chart now runs one `pre-install,pre-upgrade` hook Job, `<release>-kagent-namespace` (weight -8, `alpine/k8s`, as the hook ServiceAccount, whose own hook events gain `pre-install,pre-upgrade` while this hook renders): it creates the namespace when it is missing, waits out one that is still terminating (the reinstall right after an uninstall), and leaves an existing one alone. The `Namespace` is deliberately not an object of the meta release — the connectivity release renders and tracks it, adopting the hook-created one exactly as it adopts the one Giant Swarm's bases pre-create, and two Helm releases must never track one object. Not rendered with the engine off (the fleet's pure render is byte-identical; a cluster's own Flux gets the namespace out of band), with kagent off, with `kagent.namespaceOverride` empty or equal to the `HelmRelease`s' target namespace. Measured on kind (kagent on, no namespace): `helm install --wait` deployed, `helm upgrade` idempotent, `helm uninstall --wait` clean with the namespace gone through the connectivity release, reinstall clean. `make verify-engine` asserts the hook and its absences; the ATS kind smoke can turn kagent on from this version.
